ἡμιτρίγωνος.definition: hyperdor. forming half a triangle, of the triangles made by drawing a perpendicular from an angle of an equilateral triangle, Speus. ap. Theol.Ar.63: neut. as Subst., Ti.Locr.98a, Simp.in Cael.561.13

ἡμιτριταῖος.definition: half every three days, of a semi-tertian fever, Hp.Epid.1.2, Gal.17.233

ἡμίτριτον.definition: the sixth part , Inscr. on a weight, CIG8535

ἡμίφλεκτος.definition: half-burnt, App.BC5.88, Luc.DDeor.13.2; by love, Theoc.2.133; half-cooked, Hp.Epid.2.6.29

ἡμίφωνος.definition: half-pronounced, Aristaenet.1.10; Subst. a semi-vowel, as Arist.Po.1456b27, Phld.Po.2.16, D.H.Comp.14, D.T.631.16, etc

ἡμιφωσώνιον.definition: a kind of garment, Ar.Fr.784; cf

ἡμίχιον.definition: a measure, half a PCair.Zen.12.17 , etc

ἡμιχοίνικος.definition: holding a a half- Thphr.HP8.4.5, Dsc.5.72

ἡμίχοον.definition: Id.Int.42 , Arist.HA627b3); also IG11.199 B80 ; Hp.Morb.3.17: contr. Arist.Ath.69.2, IG12.188.22, PAmh.2.93.12

ἡμιχώριον.definition: half of an office or liturgy jointly undertaken, POxy.1413.1

ἡμίψυκτος.definition: half-dried, Str.15.1.18:—also Gp.2.27.9; half-cooled, Dsc.3.86, cf. Paul.Aeg.3.54

ἡμιωβελιαῖος.definition: costing or worth half an obol, PCair.Zen.19.5 :—less correctly written Ar.Ra.554; as large as a half- obol, X.Mem.1.3.12

ἡμιωβέλιον.definition: half-obol, IG12.6.90, Eup.154, Aeschin.Socr.41, Arist.Rh.1374b26, IG11..287 A40 , etc.:—less correctly X.An.1.5.6 codd., Arist.Fr.589 codd. Poll., Thphr.Char.6.9, Dsc.4.175: Thphr.Lap.46 , Sor.1.63 , Hdn.Epim.204: Dor…

ἡμιωριαῖος.definition: lasting half an hour: neut. as Subst., Phlp.in Ph.802.15

ἡμιώριον.definition: = Men.1015, Str.2.5.36, Hipparch.2.4.2, Cleom.1.6, Apoc.8.1 , Dsc.1.33

ἠμύω.definition: aor. : pf. part; trans., cause to fall, ruin, Musae.Fr.22. , but ib.7.715 ; cf

ἠνεμόφοιτος.definition: walking on the wind, Nonn.D.2.24; ib.37.85

ἡνιοστρόφος.definition: charioteer, S.El.731. II. Pass., guided by reins, A.Ch.1022; Pass., guided by reins, A.Ch.1022

ἡνιοχεία.definition: chariot- driving, Id.Grg.516e, al.: pl., Id.Lg.795a; Hdn.1.13.8: generally, conduct, management, Plu.2.966f

ἡνιοχεύς.definition: Ep. poet. for Il.5.505; 312, cf. APl.5.337; the constellation Auriga, Nonn.D.1.178, al

ἡνιοχεύω.definition: Dor. poet. form of act as charioteer, Il.11.103, cf. 23.641, Od.6.319: metaph., direct, guide, . . Alex.Aet.2: c. gen., Anacr.4: c. acc., IG3.82a

ἡνιοχέω.definition: Lacon. , prose form of hold the reins, . . higher up or lower down, i.e. longer or shorter, X.Eq.7.10: c. acc., drive, Hdt.4.193; Luc.DDeor.12.2: metaph., Ar.V.1022; Luc.Am.37; . . Epigr.Gr.922 ; Lib.Ep.987.5; Plu.2.1…

Ἡνιόχη.definition: fem. of a name of Hera, Paus.9.39.5

ἠπάομαι.definition: mend, repair , Gal.Thras.25: abs., Id.UP3.1:—Med., aor. 1 inf. Hes.Fr.172; Ar.Fr.227; Gal.Thras.5: pf. part. Pass., Aristid.2.307 J., cf. BCH51.326

ἡπατίζω.definition: to be liver-coloured, Dsc.3.22; suffer from hepatic dropsy, Diocl.Fr.46

ἡπάτιον.definition: Dim. of a common dish at Athens, Ar.Fr.506, Alc.Com.25, Alex.110.16, PLond.3.1259.36 , etc

ἡπατῖτις.definition: of or in the liver; liver-coloured, Gp.6.6.2, Alex.Trall.7.6; hepatitis [gemma], Plin.HN37.186

ἡπατοσκοπέω.definition: inspect the liver for soothsaying, LXXEz.21.21

ἡπατόσκοπος.definition: inspecting the liver, soothsaying, Artem.2.69; Hsch. s.v

ἡπατοφαγέομαι.definition: Pass., to have one's liver eaten, S.E.M.1.286

ἤπειρος.definition: Dor. terra firma, land; esp. the mainland of Western Greece, opp. the neighbouring islands, Od.14.97, al.; 18.84, cf. Th.3.114 : generally, mainland, opp. islands, Hdt.1.148,171, al., Th.1.5, Philostr.VA1.20, etc

ἠπειρόω.definition: to make into mainland, opp. Arist.Mu.400a28; AP9.670:—Pass., to become so, Th.2.102, Ph.2.511

ἠπειρώτης.definition: Subst. dweller on the mainland, opp. Hdt.6.49, cf. 1.171, Isoc.4.132: fem. Adj., opp. to those in islands, Hdt.1.151, cf. 7.109, Th.1.5, al.; also alliance with a military power, opp. ib.35, cf. 4.12; Id.6.86

ἠπεροπεύς.definition: Ep. = Od.11.364; of Bacchus, AP9.524.8; of dreams, A.R.3.617

ἠπεροπευτής.definition: a cheat, deceiver, of Paris , Il.3.39, cf.h.Merc.282, etc

ἠπεροπεύω.definition: Ep. Verb, used only in pres. and impf., cheat, cajole: c. acc. pers., esp. of seduction, Il.5.349; Od.15.421; so of Aphrodite, Il.3.399: generally, 23.605, Od.14.400, 15.419; 13.327, Hes.Op.55

ἠπεροπηΐς.definition: pecul. fem. of cheating arts, [Hom.] ap. Str.1.2.4, etc

ἠπητής.definition: repairer, mender, Batr.184, POxy.2149.21 , v.l. in X.Cyr.1.6.16; condemned by Phryn.73; Sammelb.3939, cf. 3962: —fem. needlewoman, UPZ91.16 , POxy.1679.5 , Hsch

ἤπητρον.definition: in pl., mender's wages, POxy. 736.10 , PTeb.120 Intr

ἠπιαλέω.definition: have a fever or ague, Ar.Ach.1165 , Arist.Pr.947b21

ἠπιάλης.definition: = nightmare, personified in Sophr.68: acc. Id.70: Hdn.Gr.2.518; cf. sq

ἠπίαλος.definition: ague, Thgn.174, Gal.7.347; = foreg., nightmare, Ar.V.1038, as expld. by Did. ap.Sch

ἠπιόδωρος.definition: soothing by gifts, bountiful, fond, Il.6.251; Stesich.26; Opp.H.4.7, etc

ἠπιόχειρ.definition: with soothing hand, AP9.525.8, prob. in Orph.H.23.8, 84.8

ἠπιόω.definition: intr., feel easier, Hp.Epid.5.20 :—Pass., to be softened, Phld. Mus.p.33 K.: aor. Sch.Il.1.146

ἠπύω.definition: Dor. and Arc. IG5.6.3 (Tegea, iv; abs., of the wind, roar, Il.14.399; of the lyre, sound, Od.17.271; sing, Pi.O.5.19: c.acc. cogn., Mosch.2.124

Ἡρακλείτειος.definition: of Heraclitus, Pl.R.498b; his disciples, Id.Tht.179e, D.L.9.6

Ἡρακλειτίζω.definition: to be a follower of Heraclitus, Arist.Metaph.1010a11

ἠρεμάζω.definition: to be still, silent, esp. from grief, LXX2 Es.9.3

ἠρεμαῖος.definition: quiet, gentle, Pl.Lg.734a; Id.Plt.307a; a slight fever, Hp.Mul.1.38; opp. Pl.Lg.733c: Comp., Plu.Sol.31: irreg., X.Cyr.7.5.63, Thphr.Vent.29. Adv. = X.Eq.9.5, Gp.12.14.1: Comp. Arist.Mete.368a12; X.Cyr.3.1.30

ἠρεμέω.definition: hyperdor. Ti.Locr.95d:—to be still; to be unmoved, remain fixed, Pl.Grg.527b, cf. Lg.891a

ἠρέμησις.definition: hyperdor. Ti.Locr.104b:—rest, opp. Arist.Ph.251a26, al.; Id.de An.407a32; of Ti.Locr. l.c

ἠρεμί.definition: Adv. for Ar.Ra.315, v.l. in Aristaenet.1.22

ἠρεμία.definition: rest, opp. Arist.Ph.202a4; of the mind, quietude, Pl.Def.412a, cf. Arist.de An.406a27 ; leaving you entirely at rest, v.l. for D.13.8

ἠρεμίζω.definition: bring to rest, stop, X.Eq.7.18; intr., = X.Lac.1.3

ἤρεμος.definition: later form for quiet; smoothness, of pigments, Thphr.Lap.62

ἠριγένεια.definition: early-born, child of; bearing in spring, A.Fr.426

ἠριγενής.definition: = epith. of A.R.3.1224: abs., = Id.2.450; a day, Orph.Fr.275

ἠριγέρων.definition: early-old, name of groundsel, from its hoary down, Senecio vulgaris, Thphr.HP7.7.1, Dsc.4.96

ἠρυγγίς.definition: of or belonging to the Nic.Al.564

ἤρυγγος.definition: eryngo, Eryngium creticum, Id.Th.645,849; goat's beard, Arist.HA610b29

ἥρῳ.definition: poet. dat. sg. of gen. and acc. of same

ἡρωίαμβος.definition: poem consisting of hexameters and iambics, Tz.H.4.868

ἡρωίζω.definition: write heroic verse or an epic poem, Eust.4.1

ἡρωισμός.definition: worship of heroes, IG12.29 :— hence IG22.1339 ; Annuario 4/5.482; BCH50.15 , 22.255 : later

ἡρωίνη.definition: fem. of heroine, Theoc.13.20; a deceased woman , CIG2259 , IG3.889; of a deified Empress, Jul.Caes.334b

ἡρωίς.definition: = I, Id.P.11.7, Call.Fr.126. 2. = II, IG12.51 , Rev.Phil.36.55 , AJP48.33 . II. as fem. of A.R.1.1048; Epic, AP9.504. 2. nine-yearly festival at Delphi, Plu.2.293c

ἡρωολογία.definition: tale of heroes, title of work by Anaximander, Ath.11.498b

ἡσσάομαι.definition: as a real Pass., to be defeated, discomfited, Hdt.3.106, And.4.28, Th.2.39; Pl.Phdr.233c, Plt.305c, etc.; Id.Lg.650a: c. gen. pers., E.Hec.1252, Ar.Av.70, Th.3.57, etc.: c. gen. rei, Herod. l.c.: c. dat. modi, Hdt.5.4…

ἡσσητέος.definition: neut. pl. one must be beaten, by a woman, S.Ant.678, cf. Ar.Lys.450

ἡσυχάζω.definition: with or without a fallacy, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.8 , Gell.1.2.4; trans., bring to rest, Pl.R.572a

ἡσυχαῖος.definition: Dor. = S.OC197 ; X.Eq.9.6; gentle, Pl.Plt.307a; of persons, E.Med.808; at rest, of the embryo, Pl.Lg.775c; peace, tranquillity, S.Fr.941.6; E.Fr.552.4: neut. as Adv., Thphr.Sign.52,53; prob.in ib.54

ἡσυχάστρια.definition: she who soothes, gloss on Hsch., Suid., cf.EM59.35

ἡσυχία.definition: Ion. Dor. , rest; silence, stillness, E.Alc.77 ; esp. of the Pythagoreans, Luc.Vit.Auct.3

ἡσύχιος.definition: Dor. , = still, quiet, at rest, Il.21.598; Pi.P.9.22; also in Prose, of a quiet disposition, Hdt.1.107; Pl.Chrm.160b; ib. c; Id.R.604e; Antipho3.2.1; Th.1.120: Comp. more reposeful, Phld.Rh. 2.60S. Adv. h.Merc.438, Pl…

ἡσυχόομαι.definition: Pass., keep quiet, be at rest, Aq.Am.6.10

ἥσυχος.definition: quiet, gentle, of character, in Comp. A.Eu.223, cf. E.Supp.952, etc.; Id.Med.217; A.Supp.199; S.Ant.1089; moderate thy wrath, E.Ba.647; their accustomed quietness, Th.6.34; less severe, Id.3.82

ἤτω.definition: late form for 3sg. imper. of , IG3.3509, BGU 419.13 , etc

Ἡφαιστότευκτος.definition: wrought by Hephaestus, S.Ph.987, cf. Simon.202A, D.L.1.32:—also A.Fr.69

ἠχέω.definition: intr., sound, ring, peal, . . Hes.Th.42; Mosch.Fr.1.4; E.Supp.72 ; of metal, Hdt.4.200; Pl.Prt.329a, cf. Men.66.4; of the grasshopper, chirp, Alc.39, Theoc.16.96; of the ears, tingle, LXX1 Ki.3.11; impers., of anecho,…

ἠχή.definition: Dor. sound, noise, Il.13.837: freq. in dat., . . 2.209; of trees, 16.769; . . Hes.Sc.438; in Trag., cry of sorrow, wail, E.Med.149 , Hipp.585 , cf. Nic.Al.304; but also E.Ph.1378; Pl.Cri.54d, cf. Ti.37b; of the grassh…

ἤχημα.definition: Dor. sound, f.l. in Ph.1.444; prob.l.for E.IA1045

ἡβηδόν.definition: Adv. from the youth upwards, Hdt.1.172, cf. 6.21, Luc.Vit.Auct.14,al.; Heraclit.121; D.S.3.54, cf. D.H.2.16,al

ἡγιασμένως.definition: Adv. pf. Pass., in holy manner, Al.Ps.133.2

ἤγουν.definition: Conj., that is to say, or rather, to define a word more correctly, freq. in glosses, cf. Eust.50.15, Lyd.Mens.4.23, etc.: sts. introduced into the text, . . Hp.Acut. 49 ; X.Oec.19.11: in late Prose, or at any rate, PM…

ἠδελφισμένως.definition: Adv. pf. Pass., prop. with brotherly likeness: metaph., just as if.., Hp.Mul.1.3: abs., in like manner, ib.2.205

ἤδη.definition: already, by this time, 'tis already night, Il.7.282; ib.402: with numerals, Od.2.89; Pl.Prt.309d; S.Ph.312; ib.354; Id.El.726; Id.Aj.1402

ἡδομένως.definition: Adv. of foreg., with joy, gladly, X.Cyr.8.4.9

ἠθροισμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of gloss on Hsch

ἦκα.definition: of Place or Motion, slightly, a little, a little to the left, Il.23.336; Od.20.301: hence, generally, softly, gently, 18.94, cf. 92; Il.24.508; 20.440; Od.17.254; Nic.Al.226

ἠκριβωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of exactly, Aristeas310, Eust.1406.29

ἤλιθα.definition: Adv. very much, exceedingly; in vain, to no purpose, Call.Lav.Pall.124, A.R.2.283; Nic.Al.25, cf. 140

ἠλληγορημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., allegorically, Tz.ad Hes.Op.56

ἡμαρτημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of faultily, Pl.Men.88e; Id.Lg.670c, Iamb.VP33.233

ἠμελημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of in a state of neglect, Isoc.Ep.8.10; X.Mem.3.11.4; Arr.Ind.20.3; with studied neglect, D.C.51.12; carelessly, Max.Tyr.28.5

ἠμέν.definition: Ep. Conj., correl. to , both . . and . . , Il.2.789, etc.; 5.751; sts. is added to 5.128; Od.2.268; . . . . Il.1.453: rarely folld. by or . . . . . 12.428; . . Od.8.575: more freq. by Il.15.664,670, Hes.Op.339

ἡμερολεγδόν.definition: Adv., bycount of days, A.Pers.63; to the very day, Arist.HA575a27

ἡμιρρόπως.definition: Adv. half turning the scale, i.e. lightly, gently, opp. Hp.Epid.2.1.7

ἡμισάκις.definition: Adv. half a time, Iamb.inNic.p.14P.,al.; two and a half times, Papp.556.16

ἠμφισβητημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., in a questionable manner, dub. in Phld.Rh.Supp.p.56 S

ἠναγκασμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., perforce, D.H.Pomp.3

ἠναντιωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., in opposite ways, Phld.Mus.p.103 K

ᾐνιγμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., as in a riddle, obscurely, Plot.6.2.22

ἡνωμένως.definition: Adv.pf.part. Pass., in one word , Procl.in Prm.p.525S.; in a unity, Id.in Euc.p.138 F., Dam.Pr.1; together, HeroGeom.12.53

ἠπειγμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., hurriedly, Hsch

ἡπλωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., gloss on prob. in Hsch

ἠραιωμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., gloss on Sch.Opp.H.1.547

ἠρέμα.definition: on the stage, aside, in a stage-whisper, Sch.E.Hec.1023, Or.671, Sch.A.Ch.46

ἦρι.definition: Ep. Adv. early, Il.9.360; Od.20.156; 19.320; in the morning, Schwyzer789 . cf

ᾐρμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., loftily, Poll.9.147

ἡρμοσμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., fitly, D.S.17.19

ἠσκημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., in a practised manner, Poll.1.157

ἡσσόνως.definition: Adv. of sq., J.AJ17.5.5, 18.2.4, 19.1.15, prob. in Hp.Art.69

ἡσυχῇ.definition: PCair.Zen. ), Dor. Adv. stilly, quietly, softly, gently, Pi.P.11.55, etc.; Ar.Pl.692; E.Hipp.444; keep quiet! Pl.Hp.Ma.298c; to keep it still, X.Cyn.3.4; Pl.Phd.115c; Id.Chrm.159b, etc.; to recollect quietly, at one’s…

ηὐξημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., gloss on Eust.769.23

ἠΰτε.definition: Ep. Particle, as, like as, Il.2.872, etc.; B.12.87; freq. in similes, Il.1.359, 2.87, etc.: after a Comp., [the cloud] appears to him while afar off very black, even as pitch, 4.277, v. Sch.; with sobs coming quicker …

ηὐτοματισμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass., arbitrarily, Procl.in Prm.p.650 S

ἧχι.definition: Ep. for Adv. where, Il.1.607, Call.Ap.91, etc.; D.P.176,258; Id.67

ἠῶθεν.definition: Dor. Adv., from morn, i.e. at dawn; to-morrow morning, Od.15.506; in the morning, A.R.4.1224
